rationale: The candidate is a coherent single mass in all four views, but it remains a generic boxy bar with shallow roof articulation and only a very weak ground response to the access edge. The top view shows two narrow separations in the roof/plan, but they do not read as a usable court or public void, and the mass does not clearly open toward the verified frontage. Across views there is no convincing section program logic for neighborhood living beyond a compact envelope; it lacks an active threshold, a legible public void, and any meaningful upper-vs-ground hierarchy. The silhouette is not disastrous, but it is too close to a sealed extrusion to satisfy the brief. The strongest transferable move from references is to preserve the compact bar as anchor, then carve a substantial court/notch or split-wing opening aligned to the access edge while keeping the upper mass calm.
